42.0.s.en: 1. The chosen servant of the Lord:

42.0.0.en: 1 “Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth; I have put my spirit upon him: he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles. 2 He shall not cry, nor lift up, nor cause his voice to be heard in the street. 3 A bruised reed shall he not break, and the smoking flax shall he not quench: he shall bring forth judgment unto truth. 4 He shall not fail nor be discouraged, till he have set judgment in the earth: and the isles shall wait for his law.”

42.0.1.en: The song here presents to us the person of the chosen Servant, who is the Lord Christ Himself, for it says in it:

42.0.2.en: First: “Behold my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delighteth” [1]. It is not strange that the Messiah is called “the servant of Jehovah” or “the servant of the Lord,” though He is His Word, begotten eternally and one with Him in the same divine essence. Rather, by His divine love He longed to descend to our servitude in order to carry us to His glories, and as a representative of us He obeyed the Father unto death, even the death of the cross, so that He might accomplish our salvation and establish us in Him, that we may be counted obedient and become the object of the Father’s good pleasure (Eph 1:3-5).

42.0.3.en: If the Father chose His only-begotten Son to accomplish salvation, declaring the perfection of divine love, then when we enter into Him and enjoy membership in His body, we too become chosen by the Son, the object of His love and delight!

42.0.4.en: The word “my chosen” does not mean the choosing of one from among many; rather it points to the greatness of the Father toward the Messiah. As the Lord Christ Himself says: “As the Father hath loved me, so have I loved you: continue ye in my love” (Jn 15:9); “that the love wherewith thou hast loved me may be in them, and I in them” (Jn 17:26). This love is portrayed by the words: “in whom my soul delighteth” [1]. For all the Father’s delight in Him is eternal, and was declared at the Lord’s baptism and transfiguration and throughout the stages of His saving works.

42.0.5.en: The Evangelist Matthew quoted what is stated here in [1-3] as an explicit prophecy about the Lord Christ (Mt 12:17-21), affirming the following points:

42.0.6.en: a. The one chosen to accomplish salvation.

42.0.7.en: b. In Him is the Father’s delight in us.

42.0.8.en: c. The desire and hope of the Gentiles.

42.0.9.en: d. By meekness He grants victory.

42.0.10.en: e. He deals tenderly with every weak one.

42.0.11.en: St. Augustine comments on this text, saying: [The expression “my servant” refers to the form of a servant, in which the Most High emptied Himself... The Holy Spirit was given to Him, and this was declared in the form of a dove, as the Evangelist testified (Jn 1:32). He brought forth judgment (truth) to the Gentiles, for He declared to them what was hidden from them. In His humility He does not cry out, without ceasing to proclaim the truth. His voice was not heard; those who are outside do not hear it, for those who are outside His body did not obey Him. He did not break the Jews themselves who persecuted Him, though they were a bruised reed that had lost its balance, nor did He quench them, though they were a smoking flax, for He forgave them. He came to be judged, not to judge.]

42.0.12.en: Our Christ, of whom it was said: “my chosen, in whom my soul delighteth,” came that we may realize that in Him we are chosen by the Father, the object of His delight and love, as the Apostle Paul says: “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ: according as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will” (Eph 1:3-5).

42.0.13.en: Second: “I have put my spirit upon him” [1]. The Messiah is the Word of the Father, one with Him and equal to Him in the same essence; therefore the Holy Spirit, who is the Spirit of the Father, is also the Spirit of the Son. The Holy Spirit is not a stranger to the Son; He enjoys Him without measure and without separation. The Holy Spirit is He who sanctified the womb of the Virgin Mary to accomplish the divine Incarnation, and He never departed from the Son; He led the Lord Christ up to the mountain to enter the decisive battle with the devil on the mountain of temptation... He is the Spirit whom He gave to His disciples for the pastoral work in Christ Jesus, and the Spirit whom He gave to the whole Church on the day of Pentecost, that He might sustain it in witness to Him, in worship and in daily life. Thereby He fulfilled what He promised in His farewell discourses (Jn 14:16-18, 26; 15:26; 16:7-8, 13, 14). And as St. Clement of Alexandria says: [The Instructor creates man from dust, renews him with water, and makes him grow by the Spirit].

42.0.14.en: St. Basil tells us about the work of the Holy Spirit in us, saying: [Through the Holy Spirit we regained our dwelling in Paradise, our ascent to the Kingdom of Heaven, our return to divine adoption, our boldness to call God “our Father,” our participation in the grace of Christ, our being called children of light, our right to eternal glory, and in one word, our obtaining the fullness of blessing in this age and in the age to come].

42.0.15.en: Third: “He shall bring forth truth to the Gentiles” [1]. Though the Lord disciplined the Gentiles, He came to them as “the Truth,” that they might receive Him into their lives as a mystery of eternal salvation, for He says: “I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me” (Jn 14:6).

42.0.16.en: * Christ dwells in the inner man, as the Apostle says (Eph 3:16-17), and to the inner man belongs the vision of the truth, for He said: “I am the truth” (Jn 14:6).

42.0.17.en: * He Himself is the life, and He Himself is the truth. Let Him come and save us... to separate the wheat from the tares!

42.0.18.en: St. Augustine * I cry out with a calm and quiet voice, saying: O You who are hidden within me and concealed, reveal within me Your hidden mystery, disclose to me Your beauty that is within me. O You who built me a temple for Your dwelling, overshadow me with the cloud of Your glory within Your temple.

42.1.0.en: The Spiritual Elder Fourth: “He shall not cry, nor lift up, nor cause his voice to be heard in the street” [2]. For He came to proclaim the voice of practical, quiet love through self-giving unto the cross; His pulpit is the cross, and His words are the wounds of His body that speak of love.

42.1.1.en: The Word of God came to us to teach us the life of true action that springs from love, with the quietness and calm of the soul in it, instead of being occupied with many glittering words and deceiving outward appearances. The divine Word taught us how to speak through love and practical life, so that He Himself may shine forth in us!

42.1.2.en: * If you are silent, you will have peace wherever you live.

42.1.3.en: Father Piamun * I have often spoken and regretted it, but of silence I have never once regretted.

42.2.0.en: St. Arsenius Fifth: “A bruised reed shall he not break, and the smoking flax shall he not quench: he shall bring forth judgment unto truth” [3].

42.2.1.en: Our Christ came to the broken souls to awaken hope in them; He does not wound the feelings of sinners, nor flatter them. He speaks the truth with love so as to bind up every inflamed wound and to support every weary soul.

42.2.2.en: * Jesus had compassion on us, so as not to frighten us away from Him but to call us to Him; He came in meekness and in humility... and thereby He said: “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest” (Mt 11:28). Thereby the Lord refreshed us and did not shut us in or drive us away...

42.2.3.en: * We must know that God is a God of mercy, inclined to pardon rather than to severity; therefore it was said: “I desired mercy, and not sacrifice” (Hos 6:6)...

42.2.4.en: * When you refuse to accept repentance, you are in effect saying: “No wounded man shall enter our inn, and no one shall be healed in our Church. We do not care for the sick, for we are all healthy, and we have no need of a physician, because He Himself said: ‘They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.’”

42.2.5.en: * Send, O Lord, to the streets of the city, and gather the good and the bad, and bring into Your Church the weak, the blind and the lame (Lk 14:21). Command, O Lord, that Your house be filled, bringing them (the sinners) to Your banquet, for You create those who follow You when You call them...

42.2.6.en: * May no one fear perishing, whatever his condition and however great his fall, for the good Samaritan of the Gospel will pass by, and we find him going down from Jerusalem to Jericho... This good Samaritan is a symbol of the Lord Christ, the keeper of souls; He will not leave you but will have compassion on you and heal you. The good Samaritan (= keeper) did not leave the one who was lying between living and dead, for he saw in him breaths of life, and hoped for his healing.

42.3.0.en: St. Cyprian Sixth: “He shall not fail nor be discouraged, till he have set judgment in the earth: and the isles shall wait for his law” [4].

42.3.1.en: Our Christ was marked by practical love and meekness; in His love He opens the doors of hope before sinners, however great their evils. This is unlike the man who is harsh with his brother and counts himself more righteous than he, and closes the door before many. This meek divine love is accompanied by divine work without ceasing unto death, even the death of the cross, and in this He was not broken but was glorified by the Resurrection, and declared the truth by accomplishing salvation.

42.3.2.en: Some scholars try to interpret the word “isles” here as Europe, the United States of America or Australia.

42.4.s.en: 2. The call of the servant of the Lord:

42.4.0.en: 5 Thus saith God the LORD, he that created the heavens, and stretched them out; he that spread forth the earth, and that which cometh out of it; he that giveth breath unto the people upon it, and spirit to them that walk therein: 6 “I the LORD have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thine hand, and will keep thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles; 7 To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house. 8 “I am the LORD: that is my name: and my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images. 9 Behold, the former things are come to pass, and new things do I declare: before they spring forth I tell you of them.”

42.4.1.en: In His love God created the heavens and the earth for the sake of man [5], and here He calls the Son who became man to establish Him as a covenant of the people and a light of the Gentiles [6], to open the inner insight to behold the Kingdom of God, and to free the captives in the prison of eternal darkness to live in the freedom of the glory of the children of God [7].

42.4.2.en: What does the calling of the servant of the Lord “a covenant” mean? As the Son of God who became the Son of Man, He was able to reconcile the Father with humanity in the body of His humanity; in Him the Father saw humanity sanctified and qualified for sonship to Him, so He declared His eternal fatherhood toward it in His only-begotten Son, and in Him humanity saw the love of the Father who gave His only Son for its salvation, that it might find a portion for itself in the Father’s bosom. This is the covenant that was established in Christ Jesus, which He sealed with His precious blood on the wood of the cross. Therefore He was called “the messenger of the covenant” (Mal 3:1).

42.4.3.en: Trypho the Jew tried to interpret what is stated here about the covenant and the light of the Gentiles as pertaining to the Mosaic Law, and St. Justin the Martyr replied to him, saying: [that if the Law were able to give enlightenment to the Gentiles and to those who received it, what need would there be to speak of a new covenant? But since God had declared beforehand that He would bring a new covenant and an everlasting law and an everlasting commandment, this is not to be understood of the old Law but of Christ and those who believe in Him, that is, of us who were of the Gentiles and have enjoyed enlightenment. The Lord says: “In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped thee: and I will preserve thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, to establish the earth, to cause to inherit the desolate heritages” (Isa 49:8). What is the inheritance (possession) of Christ? Are they not the Gentiles? What is the covenant of God but the Lord Christ? As it is said in another place: “Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee. Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and thy dominion (thy possessions) unto the uttermost parts of the earth” (Ps 2:7).]

42.5.0.en: Again St. Justin the Martyr comments on the divine saying: “I am the LORD: that is my name: and my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images” [8] thus: [I say (to the Jews): Do you not realize, my friends, that God gives glory to the one whom He has set as a light to the Gentiles, and does not give it to another?]. Thus whatever glories the Son the Savior receives, the Holy Trinity receives, being the one God in essence and divinity.

42.5.1.en: “And give thee for a covenant of the people” [6].

42.5.2.en: We have previously studied the role of the “covenant” among primitive tribes and in the Old Testament and finally in the New Testament, where the Lord Christ gave His mystical blood in the cup as a new covenant for His believers to partake of. This blood, being the sacrifice of Christ, is able to establish a compact between the Father and man, to grant us a heavenly spiritual kinship, so that we are truly counted as sons firmly established in the only-begotten Son; through it we enjoy the life-giving heavenly banquet.

42.5.3.en: Father Theodoret says: [In our partaking of the elements of the Bridegroom and drinking His blood we enter with Him into a conjugal union].

42.5.4.en: “And give thee... for a light of the Gentiles” [6]; for Christ is the divine Light who opens our inner insight that we may behold the light. Therefore the Psalmist says: “In thy light, O Lord, shall we see light,” and the Evangelist says:

42.5.5.en: “That was the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world” (Jn 1:9).

42.5.6.en: * “O send out thy light and thy truth: let them lead me; let them bring me unto thy holy hill, and to thy tabernacles” (Ps 43:3).

42.5.7.en: “Light” and “truth” are in reality two names expressing one (God). For what is the divine light but the divine truth? And the divine truth but the divine light? And the Hypostasis of Christ is both.

42.5.8.en: “I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness” (Jn 8:12); “I am the way, the truth, and the life” (Jn 14:6). He Himself is the light, and He is also the truth. Let Him come, then, and save us....

42.5.9.en: * My God... You are my light; open my eyes so that they may behold Your divine splendor, that I may be able to walk in my way without stumbling in the snares of the enemy.

42.5.10.en: Truly, how can I avoid his snares unless I see them?!

42.5.11.en: And how can I see them unless I am enlightened by Your light...?!

42.5.12.en: You are the light for the children of light! Your day knows no sunset! Your day shines for Your children so that they do not stumble!

42.5.13.en: But those who are outside of You walk in darkness and live in it!..

42.5.14.en: St. Augustine * I behold one lamp, and by its light I am illumined, and now I am in amazement, rejoicing spiritually, for within me is the fountain of life, that which is the goal of the world that is not perceived by the senses!

42.6.0.en: 10 Sing unto the LORD a new song, and his praise from the end of the earth, ye that go down to the sea, and all that is therein; the isles, and the inhabitants thereof. 11 Let the wilderness and the cities thereof lift up their voice, the villages that Kedar doth inhabit: let the inhabitants of Sela sing, let them shout from the top of the mountains. 12 Let them give glory unto the LORD, and declare his praise in the islands. 13 The LORD shall go forth as a mighty man, he shall stir up jealousy like a man of war: he shall cry, yea, roar; he shall prevail against his enemies.

42.6.1.en: “Sing unto the LORD a new song, and his praise from the end of the earth” [10]. What is this song, marked by newness, that men utter from the end of the earth, but the song of the redeemed who come from all nations, kindreds, peoples and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb... “And they cry with a loud voice, saying, Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb” (Rev 7:10). A new song because it grants unceasing renewal through “the new life which is in Christ.”

42.6.2.en: The following is noted in this song:

42.6.3.en: a. A new song that never grows old or aged, for it expresses the enjoyment of the life of heavenly joy that does not grow old. Thus the sighs of creation are turned into fellowship in the praise of the heavenly ones.

42.6.4.en: b. A universal song that includes members from the end of the earth, revealing the joy of the dwellers of the earth, the seas, and the inhabitants of the isles [10]. It springs from the depths of the inner heart and not from outward circumstances; therefore the believer practices it wherever he may be, on land or sea, in the wilderness or in a city or a village or a cave on a mountaintop [10-11].

42.7.0.en: c. The secret of the joy is the Lord Christ going before the ranks as the leader of the spiritual battle, “he shall cry, yea, roar; he shall prevail against his enemies” [13]. It is the song of victory and triumph in Christ, who cries out in victory over the devil and all his evil powers.

42.8.0.en: 14 “I have been silent from of old; I have kept still; I have restrained myself. Like a woman giving birth I cry out; I blow and snort together. 15 I lay waste the mountains and hills, and dry up all their herbs; and I make the rivers dry land, and dry up the pools. 16 And I lead the blind in a way that they knew not; in paths that they have not known I make them walk. I make darkness light before them, and crooked things straight. These things I do, and I do not forsake them. 17 They are turned back; they shall be greatly ashamed that trust in graven images, that say to the molten images, Ye are our gods!

42.8.1.en: The secret of our praise is the emptying out of the works of the old man from our depths through our receiving the works of the new man in Christ Jesus... a matter so exceedingly astonishing that it was said, “I have been silent from of old; I have kept still; I have restrained myself” [14].

42.8.2.en: He likens the leaving of the old man and the enjoyment of the new man to the woman who gives birth: she cries out from pain but brings forth a new human being; so we enjoy, through the Lord Christ, as it were the bringing forth of a new world within us: “Like a woman giving birth I cry out; I blow and snort together” [14].

42.9.0.en: He also likens the great and small nations to the mountains and hills whose herbage He dries up [15], drying up their love for earthly things, which are like the perishing grass. He also likens them to rivers that He makes dry [15]... Thus He removes their old waters to give them the living water.

42.10.0.en: Again He likens them to the blind who walk in darkness; they need the removal of blindness and darkness so as to enjoy the light and walk in the new, true spiritual way instead of walking in crooked paths, for He says: “And I lead the blind in a way that they knew not; in paths that they have not known I make them walk; I make darkness light before them and crooked things straight” [16].

42.11.s.en: 5. A call to the deaf and blind people:

42.11.0.en: 18 “Hear, ye deaf; and look, ye blind, that ye may see. 19 Who is blind, but my servant? or deaf, as my messenger that I sent? who is blind as he that is perfect, and blind as the LORD’S servant? 20 Seeing many things, but thou observest not; opening the ears, but he heareth not.” 21 The LORD is well pleased for his righteousness’ sake; he will magnify the law, and make it honourable. 22 But this is a people robbed and spoiled; they are all of them snared in holes, and they are hid in prison houses: they are for a prey, and none delivereth; for a spoil, and none saith, “Restore.” 23 Who among you will give ear to this? who will hearken and hear for the time to come? 24 Who gave Jacob for a spoil, and Israel to the robbers? did not the LORD, he against whom we have sinned? for they would not walk in his ways, neither were they obedient unto his law. 25 Therefore he hath poured upon him the fury of his anger, and the strength of battle: and it hath set him on fire round about, yet he knew not; and it burned him, yet he laid it not to heart.

42.11.1.en: Many of the Fathers see that the deaf and blind people are the Jews who did not heed the voice of the prophets concerning the Lord Christ, and their eyes were blinded from perceiving Him, so they glorified Him... The Lord chose them as His servant, but only a very few accepted faith in the Savior while the others denied Him; therefore He rebukes them, saying:

42.11.2.en: “Hear, ye deaf; and look, ye blind, that ye may see.

42.11.3.en: Who is blind, but my servant? or deaf, as my messenger that I sent?!

42.11.4.en: Who is blind as he that is perfect, and blind as the LORD’S servant?!” [18-19].

42.11.5.en: He calls them His servant because He chose them as His people devoted to Him; and also His messenger because He chose them to accept the faith and preach it as messengers proclaiming salvation and witnessing to the Gospel life; He called them “perfect” because He expected holiness in them, since He gave them every possibility for the perfect life, and indeed even for preaching the Lord Christ, the Giver of perfection.

42.12.0.en: “Seeing many things, but thou observest not” [20], for the Lord Christ came in their midst and did wonders and they saw what other peoples did not see, yet they did not observe that He is the Savior of the world, but crucified Him out of envy! They saw Him in the flesh and did not realize His true nature.

42.12.1.en: “Opening the ears, but he heareth not” [20]; they heard the prophecies as they heard the voice of the Lord Christ, yet they did not respond either to the voice of the prophets pointing toward Christ or to the voice of the Lord Himself at His coming.

42.13.0.en: The fault is in them and not in the Mosaic Law, for God magnifies the Law and makes it honourable [21]; but the enemy of good robbed the people of the depths of the Law and plundered from them the spiritual prophetic understanding, so they fell into the pit of denial and were imprisoned in the rejection of faith. The enemy of good robbed them of the enjoyment of Him to whom the Law pointed and plundered from them what the books of the Old Testament had given, and there is none to restore to them what they had lost [21-22], because they fell under the divine wrath.

42.13.1.en: The Jews hold that what is stated in this section [18-25] does not apply to them but to the idolaters or to some individuals.
